disease_label_per_paper: Early secondary syphilis (with false-positive anti-CCP and ANA); neurosyphilis diagnosed at readmission four days after discharge
presentation_summary: 29-year-old woman (G5P3) with no known medical history admitted with a 3-month history of progressive rash, night sweats, chills, lymphadenopathy, dysphagia, headache and arthralgia, plus new-onset diarrhea; pharyngitis progressed to inability to tolerate solids or liquids; treated with fluids for dehydration.
Admission vitals: BP 106/71 mmHg, pulse 108 bpm, temperature 37.4 C, SpO2 98%.

Exam: rash throughout the body including palms and soles; solitary nodules on face, neck, back and right wrist (not grouped or dermatomal); diffuse painful lymphadenopathy; generalized joint swelling and bilateral knee tenderness.
Admission aPTT 44 s. One week before admission (ED visit): CRP 184 mg/L, ESR 85 mm/h.

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: These tests revealed a positive RPR (1:128) test result.
This was followed by a positive treponemal antibody test. The patient was diagnosed with early secondary syphilis.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Rheumatologic serology on admission (autoantibody panel): anti-CCP 45 U/mL, ANA 1:320, RF 12 IU/mL, anti-dsDNA 1.0 IU/mL
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: the patients' laboratory studies also resulted in positive anti-CCP (45) and ANA (1:320) results. Her other rheumatologic studies were negative, such as rheumatoid factor. [Table 1: Anti CCP (U/mL) 45; ANA 1:320; RF/dsDNA [(Ui)/mL] 12/1.0]
confirmatory_findings.note: Autoantibody serology kept non-ranking under the presentation evidence boundary (serology/antibody workup); normalized at 6 months after treatment.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Prior CMV test positive before admission (CMV antibody index 0.9 then 1.2); working diagnosis of CMV infection before syphilis was found
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: presented to the emergency department with cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection and progressive viral symptoms ... [Table 1: CMV (AI) 0.9 (1-2 months prior), 1.2 (one week prior)]

confirmatory_findings.finding: Earlier outpatient/ED workup negative: rapid strep/throat culture, rubella IgM, Lyme screen, mononucleosis screen, CBC normal; later transiently elevated AST/ALT (values not reported) that resolved; Group A strep, Lyme, chlamydia, gonorrhea, viral panel and blood culture normal
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Her initial workup included a rapid streptococcus A test with throat culture, a rubella IgM test, Lyme antibody screen, and mononucleosis screen. The patient also underwent complete blood count. At that time, all tests were within normal limits. ... her CMP showed elevated liver markers (LFTs) ... She also underwent a full viral panel and blood culture, all of which were normal. Her CMP also showed resolution of the elevated liver enzymes.

clinical_course_events.finding: Readmission 4 days after discharge with vision changes, weakness, worse throat/jaw soreness; positive neurosyphilis IgG antibody index; CSF 7 nucleated cells, VDRL negative; treated for neurosyphilis
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: Four days after discharge ... she reported vision changes, significant weakness, and enhanced soreness of her throat and jaw ... she was found to have a positive Neurosyphilis IgG antibody index and vision changes ... CSF analysis, which showed seven nucleated cells, a normal gram stain and culture, and a negative venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) test.

actual_treatment: doxycycline (penicillin shortage), then intravenous penicillin 18-24 million units/day for 14 days (neurosyphilis protocol)

outcome.source_text_value: Six months after hospitalization ... anti-CCP, C-reactive protein (CRP), and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) ... All of these laboratory values returned to normal, and the patient reported no associated symptoms.

quality_warnings: CRP and ESR were measured at an emergency department visit one week before the index admission (no admission CRP/ESR reported); recorded with day -7.
Autoantibody results (anti-CCP, ANA, RF, anti-dsDNA) and all pathogen serology (RPR, treponemal antibody, CMV antibody index) are kept non-ranking under the presentation evidence boundary.
Temperature 37.4 C on admission; 'chills' and 'night sweats' are symptom history without measured fever.
Neurosyphilis findings at readmission are clinical course, not presentation.
No PMID assigned at retrieval date.
